title: filter and reduce
objective: Use filter to keep only matching elements, and reduce to collapse an array into a single value.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Original Code Forge chapter covering idiomatic array methods beyond the book's core coverage. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Array.prototype.filter() runs a callback once per element and builds a new array containing only the elements where the callback returned true. Elements where it returned false are left out entirely — the new array can be shorter than the original, or even empty.

Array.prototype.reduce() is the most flexible of the three: it walks through the array carrying an accumulator value forward, calling (accumulator, currentElement) => newAccumulator at each step, and returns whatever the accumulator ends up as after the last element. The second argument to reduce() is the accumulator's starting value.

A common reduce() use is summing an array: numbers.reduce((total, n) => total + n, 0) starts total at 0, adds each number to it in turn, and returns the final total — no loop or extra variable needed.
explanation.rule: filter() keeps only the elements a callback approves of; reduce() folds the whole array down into one accumulated value.

feedback.correct: Correct — filter() keeps only the elements where the callback returned true, here the even numbers.
feedback.incorrect: filter() builds a new array of only the elements that satisfy the callback — n % 2 === 0 is true only for even numbers.

assignment.title: Total the Evens
assignment.brief: Write sumEvens(numbers) that returns the sum of only the even numbers in the array, using filter and reduce together (not a loop).
requirements: Use .filter() to keep only even numbers.
Use .reduce() to sum the filtered numbers, and return the total.

hints: First filter to keep only numbers where n % 2 === 0.
Then reduce the filtered array to a running total, starting at 0.
You can chain them directly: numbers.filter(...).reduce(...).
